page: Google Cloud Platform f1-micro is an entry-level shared-core compute instance positioned within the provider's general-purpose family. It provides 1 virtual CPU powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon processor with shared core allocation, backed by 0.6 GB of system RAM. The underlying processor includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 38 MB of L3 cache, along with support for vector and cryptographic instruction sets such as AVX, AVX-512F, and AES-NI. The instance includes no local storage or dedicated GPU accelerators.

Benchmark results place the instance in the bottom 10 percent of performance tiers across compute and memory workloads. The single virtual CPU scored 384.79 in stress-ng single-core and multi-core testing, alongside a PassMark CPU score of 236.08. Synthetic evaluation showed a PassMark CPU extended instructions score of 203.47 and an encryption score of 73.1. Memory metrics reflect constrained capacity, delivering 80.8 GB/sec on cached 16 KB read blocks and 0.2 GB/sec on 256 MB uncached write blocks, with zero recorded throughput on extended database operation benchmarks.

Network and application testing shows a static web serving throughput of 0.22 GB/sec and Redis SET performance reaching 0.24 million operations per second. Because physical CPU time is shared and total memory is limited to 600 MB, resource contention and memory exhaustion can occur under sustained load. The instance offers maximum cost efficiency for low-overhead tasks, making it suited strictly for lightweight utility scripts, basic microservices, minimal development environments, and low-traffic proof-of-concept deployments.
description: Google Cloud Platform f1-micro is a shared-core general-purpose instance featuring 1 vCPU on an x86_64 Intel Xeon platform paired with 0.6 GB of RAM. The instance lacks local storage, complimentary public IPv4 addresses, and hardware accelerators. Hardware extensions include AVX, AVX-512F, and AES. Empirical benchmarks demonstrate limited compute capabilities, recording 384.79 on stress-ng tests, a PassMark CPU score of 236.08, and static web serving throughput of 0.22 GB/sec. Large block uncached memory write bandwidth is measured at 0.2 GB/sec, and Redis SET throughput reaches 0.24 million operations per second. Due to its minimal memory envelope and shared execution pipeline, f1-micro is suited for background cron automation, low-volume webhook receivers, microservices, and non-production testing workloads.
